# First install package
```{r}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
  install.packages("BiocManager")

BiocManager::install("cBioPortalData")
```
# Load it
```{r}
library(cBioPortalData)
```
# Load it
```{r}
library(cbioportalR)
```
# Connect to cbioportal
```{r}
cbio <- cBioPortal()
```
# Get studies
```{r}
studies <- getStudies(cbio)
```
#Load library
```{r}
library(dplyr)
```
# Filter for prostate cancer studies
```{r}
prad_studies <- studies %>% filter(grepl("prad", studyId, ignore.case = TRUE))
View(prad_studies)
```
# Download prostate cancer data pack (may take a few minutes)
```{r}
prad_data <- cBioDataPack("prad_tcga")
```

# Load library
```{r}
library(MultiAssayExperiment)
```
# Confirm the object type and data
```{r}
class(prad_data)         # Should return: MultiAssayExperiment
names(experiments(prad_data))    # Shows all available data modalities
```
# Extract gene expression
```{r}
expr <- assays(prad_data)[["mrna_seq_v2_rsem"]]
```
# Check dimensions (genes × samples)
```{r}
dim(expr)
```
# Preview the first few genes and samples
```{r}
head(expr[, 1:5])
```
# Extract clinical data
```{r}
clinical <- colData(prad_data)
head(clinical)
```
# Remove genes with all 0s across samples
```{r}
expr_filtered <- expr[rowSums(expr) > 0, ]
dim(expr_filtered)  # Check new dimensions
```
#Quick Check on Distribution of Values to see if data is log transformed
```{r}
summary(as.vector(expr_filtered))
```
# Data not log transformed so,Apply log2 transformation
```{r}
expr_log2 <- log2(expr_filtered + 1)
summary(as.vector(expr_log2))  # Confirm new scale
```
#Scale the Data (for PCA & ML)
# Transpose: samples as rows, genes as columns
```{r}
expr_t <- t(expr_log2)
```
# Scale: mean = 0, sd = 1 (per gene/column)
```{r}
expr_scaled <- scale(expr_t)
```
# Confirm dimensions and preview
```{r}
dim(expr_scaled)
expr_scaled[1:5, 1:5]
```
# Run PCA
```{r}
pca <- prcomp(expr_scaled, center = FALSE, scale. = FALSE)
```
# View variance explained
```{r}
summary(pca)
```
#Let’s Prepare Clinical Info
## Extract Gleason scores to know if it it will give us a nice range for PCA and visuslization
```{r}
gleason <- clinical$GLEASON_SCORE
names(gleason) <- rownames(clinical)  # Ensure matching sample IDs
table(gleason, useNA = "ifany")       # Check distribution
```
# Build a PCA dataframe
```{r}
pca_df <- as.data.frame(pca$x[, 1:2])  # PC1 and PC2
pca_df$Sample <- rownames(pca_df)
pca_df$Gleason <- as.factor(gleason[rownames(pca_df)])  # add Gleason scores
```
# Load ggplot2 
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
```
# Plot
```{r}
ggplot(pca_df, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = Gleason)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8, size = 2.5) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    title = "PCA of Prostate Cancer Samples (Colored by Gleason Score)",
    x = "PC1",
    y = "PC2"
  )
```
# Fix sample ID matching: remove '-01' from expression sample IDs
```{r}
cleaned_sample_ids <- gsub("-01$", "", rownames(expr_scaled))
```
# Now match cleaned IDs to clinical data
```{r}
gleason_fixed <- clinical$GLEASON_SCORE[match(cleaned_sample_ids, clinical$SAMPLE_ID)]
```
# Create new PCA plot data frame
```{r}
pca_df <- as.data.frame(pca$x[, 1:2])
pca_df$Sample <- rownames(pca_df)
pca_df$Gleason <- as.factor(gleason_fixed)
```
# Plot again
```{r}
ggplot(pca_df, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = Gleason)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8, size = 2.5) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    title = "PCA of Prostate Cancer Samples (Colored by Gleason Score)",
    x = "PC1",
    y = "PC2"
  )
```
#check the format of the sample IDs
```{r}
head(rownames(expr_scaled))         # From expression matrix
head(clinical$SAMPLE_ID)            # From clinical metadata
```
# Direct matching using full sample IDs
```{r}
gleason_fixed <- clinical$GLEASON_SCORE[match(rownames(expr_scaled), clinical$SAMPLE_ID)]
```
# Build the PCA data frame again
```{r}
pca_df <- as.data.frame(pca$x[, 1:2])
pca_df$Sample <- rownames(pca_df)
pca_df$Gleason <- as.factor(gleason_fixed)
```
# Re-plot with corrected coloring
```{r}
ggplot(pca_df, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = Gleason)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8, size = 2.5) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    title = "PCA of Prostate Cancer Samples (Colored by Gleason Score)",
    x = "PC1",
    y = "PC2"
  )
```
##Run K-means Clustering
# Extract first 10 PCs for clustering
```{r}
pcs_for_clustering <- pca$x[, 1:10]
```
# Set number of clusters (you can test different k values)
```{r}
set.seed(42)
kmeans_result <- kmeans(pcs_for_clustering, centers = 5, nstart = 25)
```
# Add cluster assignment to PCA dataframe
```{r}
pca_df$Cluster <- as.factor(kmeans_result$cluster)
```
# Visualize PCA with clusters
```{r}
ggplot(pca_df, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = Cluster)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8, size = 2.5) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    title = "PCA of Prostate Cancer Samples (K-means Clusters)",
    x = "PC1", y = "PC2"
  )
```
##Compare Clusters vs Gleason Score
# Create a table of Cluster vs Gleason Score
```{r}
table(Cluster = pca_df$Cluster, Gleason = pca_df$Gleason)
```
#Prepare the expression matrix for the heatmap
# Use original (log2-transformed, filtered) expression matrix
# Match samples in same order as pca_df
```{r}
expr_heatmap <- expr_log2[ , rownames(pca_df) ]
```
# Calculate variance per gene
```{r}
gene_vars <- apply(expr_heatmap, 1, var)
```
# Select top 100 most variable genes
```{r}
top_genes <- names(sort(gene_vars, decreasing = TRUE))[1:100]
```
# Subset matrix
```{r}
heatmap_data <- expr_heatmap[top_genes, ]
```
# Convert to matrix for pheatmap
```{r}
heatmap_mat <- as.matrix(heatmap_data)
```
# Create annotation dataframe for samples
```{r}
ann_col <- data.frame(Cluster = pca_df$Cluster)
rownames(ann_col) <- rownames(pca_df)
```
# Load pheatmap
```{r}
if (!requireNamespace("pheatmap", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("pheatmap")
library(pheatmap)
```
# Plot heatmap
```{r}
pheatmap(heatmap_mat,
         annotation_col = ann_col,
         show_rownames = FALSE,
         show_colnames = FALSE,
         scale = "row",
         fontsize = 10,
         main = "Top 100 Variable Genes by Cluster")
```
#Show only top 30 variable genes
```{r}
top_genes_30 <- names(sort(gene_vars, decreasing = TRUE))[1:30]
heatmap_data_30 <- expr_heatmap[top_genes_30, ]
heatmap_mat_30 <- as.matrix(heatmap_data_30)

pheatmap(heatmap_mat_30,
         annotation_col = ann_col,
         show_rownames = TRUE,
         show_colnames = FALSE,
         scale = "row",
         fontsize = 10,
         main = "Top 30 Variable Genes by Cluster")
```
#Show only a subset of representative samples
# Randomly sample 100 samples for better visualization
```{r}
set.seed(123)
sample_subset <- sample(colnames(expr_heatmap), 100)

heatmap_sub <- expr_heatmap[top_genes, sample_subset]

pheatmap(as.matrix(heatmap_sub),
         annotation_col = ann_col[sample_subset, , drop=FALSE],
         show_rownames = FALSE,
         show_colnames = FALSE,
         scale = "row",
         fontsize = 10,
         main = "Top 100 Genes in 100 Samples")
```
##Supervised Machine Learning
# Convert Gleason scores to numeric
```{r}
gleason_num <- as.numeric(as.character(pca_df$Gleason))
```
# Create binary class
```{r}
gleason_binary <- ifelse(gleason_num <= 7, "Low", "High")
table(gleason_binary)
```
#Select top 500 variable genes
```{r}
top_genes_500 <- names(sort(gene_vars, decreasing = TRUE))[1:500]
expr_ml <- t(expr_log2[top_genes_500, ])  # samples as rows
```
# Create dataframe with features + label
```{r}
ml_data <- as.data.frame(expr_ml)
ml_data$GleasonGroup <- factor(gleason_binary)
```
# Split: 70% training, 30% testing
```{r}
set.seed(123)
train_index <- sample(seq_len(nrow(ml_data)), size = 0.7 * nrow(ml_data))
train_data <- ml_data[train_index, ]
test_data <- ml_data[-train_index, ]
```
#Train a Random Forest Model
# Install if not already installed
```{r}
if (!requireNamespace("randomForest", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("randomForest")
library(randomForest)
```
# Clean column names (make them syntactically valid)
```{r}
colnames(train_data) <- make.names(colnames(train_data))
colnames(test_data) <- make.names(colnames(test_data))
```
# Train the model to reasonably separate aggressive from non-aggressive tumors using transcriptomic signatures.
```{r}
set.seed(123)
rf_model <- randomForest(
  GleasonGroup ~ .,
  data = train_data,
  importance = TRUE,
  ntree = 500
)
```
# Predict and evaluate
```{r}
preds <- predict(rf_model, newdata = test_data)
conf_matrix <- table(Predicted = preds, Actual = test_data$GleasonGroup)
conf_matrix
```
# Accuracy
```{r}
accuracy <- sum(diag(conf_matrix)) / sum(conf_matrix)
paste("Accuracy:", round(accuracy * 100, 2), "%")
```
# Extract and plot top 20 important genes
# Extract importance values
```{r}
importance_df <- as.data.frame(importance(rf_model))
importance_df$Gene <- rownames(importance_df)
```
# Sort by MeanDecreaseGini
```{r}
top_genes <- importance_df %>%
  arrange(desc(MeanDecreaseGini)) %>%
  head(20)
```

# Plot
```{r}
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(top_genes, aes(x = reorder(Gene, MeanDecreaseGini), y = MeanDecreaseGini)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Top 20 Most Important Genes (Random Forest)",
    x = "Gene",
    y = "Mean Decrease Gini"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```
#Install & run ROC/AUC analysis
# Install pROC if needed
```{r}
if (!requireNamespace("pROC", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("pROC")
library(pROC)
```
# Recode the response: High = 1, Low = 0
```{r}
actual_binary <- ifelse(test_data$GleasonGroup == "High", 1, 0)
```
# Predict probabilities for class "High"
```{r}
rf_probs <- predict(rf_model, newdata = test_data, type = "prob")[, "High"]
```
# ROC curve
```{r}
roc_obj <- roc(actual_binary, rf_probs)
```
# Plot ROC
```{r}
plot(roc_obj, col = "darkorange", lwd = 3, main = "ROC Curve - Random Forest")
```
# Plot ROC and add legend in one go
```{r}
plot(roc_obj, col = "darkorange", lwd = 3, main = "ROC Curve - Random Forest")
auc_val <- auc(roc_obj)
legend("bottomright", legend = paste("AUC =", round(auc_val, 3)), col = "darkorange", lwd = 3)
```
#Train logistic regression
# Use first 10 PCs from earlier PCA
```{r}
pcs_train <- pca$x[train_index, 1:10]
pcs_test <- pca$x[-train_index, 1:10]
```
# Create dataframes for logistic model
```{r}
logit_train <- data.frame(pcs_train, GleasonGroup = train_data$GleasonGroup)
logit_test <- data.frame(pcs_test, GleasonGroup = test_data$GleasonGroup)
```
# Fit logistic regression
```{r}
logit_model <- glm(GleasonGroup ~ ., data = logit_train, family = "binomial")
```
# Predict probabilities on test set
```{r}
logit_probs <- predict(logit_model, newdata = logit_test, type = "response")
```
# Binary actual values
```{r}
actual_binary <- ifelse(logit_test$GleasonGroup == "High", 1, 0)
```
# ROC curve
```{r}
library(pROC)
logit_roc <- roc(actual_binary, logit_probs)
plot(logit_roc, col = "blue", lwd = 3, main = "ROC Curve - Logistic Regression (Top 10 PCs)")
logit_auc <- auc(logit_roc)
legend("bottomright", legend = paste("AUC =", round(logit_auc, 3)), col = "blue", lwd = 3)
```
# Re-plot ROC with AUC in one go
```{r}
plot(logit_roc, col = "blue", lwd = 3, main = "ROC Curve - Logistic Regression (Top 10 PCs)")
legend("bottomright", legend = paste("AUC =", round(logit_auc, 3)), col = "blue", lwd = 3)
```
#Support Vector Machine (SVM) with Radial Kernel
# Install e1071 if not already available
```{r}
if (!requireNamespace("e1071", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("e1071")
library(e1071)
```
# Train SVM model on top 10 PCs
```{r}
svm_model <- svm(GleasonGroup ~ ., data = logit_train, kernel = "radial", probability = TRUE)
```
# Predict probabilities
```{r}
svm_pred <- predict(svm_model, newdata = logit_test, probability = TRUE)
svm_probs <- attr(svm_pred, "probabilities")[, "High"]
```
# ROC + AUC
```{r}
svm_roc <- roc(actual_binary, svm_probs)
plot(svm_roc, col = "purple", lwd = 3, main = "ROC Curve - SVM (Top 10 PCs)")
svm_auc <- auc(svm_roc)
legend("bottomright", legend = paste("AUC =", round(svm_auc, 3)), col = "purple", lwd = 3)
```
# Prepare a dataframe with predictions
```{r}
rf_export <- data.frame(
  SampleID = rownames(test_data),
  TrueLabel = test_data$GleasonGroup,
  PredictedLabel = preds,
  Prob_High = rf_probs
)
```
# Save to CSV
```{r}
write.csv(rf_export, "rf_predictions.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
# Prepare survival input for survival analysis
# Load libraries
```{r}
library(survival)
library(survminer)
```
# Convert OS status
```{r}
clinical$OS_bin <- ifelse(grepl("DECEASED", clinical$OS_STATUS), 1, 0)
clinical$OS_time <- as.numeric(clinical$OS_MONTHS)
```
# Add RF prediction to clinical data
```{r}
clinical$PredictedRisk <- NA
clinical[rownames(test_data), "PredictedRisk"] <- preds  # "High" or "Low"
```
# Create survival object
```{r}
surv_obj <- Surv(time = clinical$OS_time, event = clinical$OS_bin)
```
# Remove "-01" suffix to match clinical rownames
```{r}
test_ids_trimmed <- gsub("-01$", "", rownames(test_data))
```
# Add predictions to matching clinical rows
```{r}
clinical$PredictedRisk <- NA
clinical[test_ids_trimmed, "PredictedRisk"] <- preds
```
# Rebuild survival object
```{r}
surv_obj <- Surv(time = clinical$OS_time, event = clinical$OS_bin)
```
# Fit Kaplan-Meier curve
```{r}
fit <- survfit(surv_obj ~ PredictedRisk, data = clinical)
```
# Plot
```{r}
ggsurvplot(fit,
           data = clinical,
           pval = TRUE,
           risk.table = TRUE,
           title = "Survival by Predicted Risk (Random Forest)",
           legend.title = "Predicted Risk",
           palette = c("steelblue", "darkorange"))
```
#GO and KEGG Enrichment Using clusterProfiler
# Install and load packages
```{r}
if (!requireNamespace("clusterProfiler", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install(c("clusterProfiler", "org.Hs.eg.db"))

library(clusterProfiler)
library(org.Hs.eg.db)
```
# Prepare gene list:get top variable genes (you already used this)
```{r}
top_genes <- names(sort(apply(expr_scaled, 2, var), decreasing = TRUE)[1:100])
```
# Convert gene symbols to gene entrez Ids
```{r}
entrez_genes <- bitr(top_genes, fromType = "SYMBOL", 
                     toType = "ENTREZID", 
                     OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db)
```
# GO enrichment
```{r}
ego <- enrichGO(gene = entrez_genes$ENTREZID,
                OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db,
                keyType = "ENTREZID",
                ont = "BP",           # Biological Process
                pAdjustMethod = "BH",
                qvalueCutoff = 0.05,
                readable = TRUE)
```
# Plot
```{r}
barplot(ego, showCategory = 15, title = "GO Enrichment - Biological Process")
```
# KEGG enrichment
```{r}
ekegg <- enrichKEGG(gene = entrez_genes$ENTREZID,
                    organism = "hsa",     # Homo sapiens
                    pvalueCutoff = 0.05)

barplot(ekegg, showCategory = 15, title = "KEGG Pathway Enrichment")
```
